title: Del norte
desc: A country you thought had one accent
setting: There is a new man at the workshop, he has said three sentences, and you have understood about half.

steps.speaker: Wilmer
steps.es: Buenas. Yo soy Wilmer, vengo de Jinotega.
steps.en: Morning. I am Wilmer, I come from Jinotega.

options.es: Mucho gusto, Wilmer. ¿De Jinotega mismo o de por ahí?
options.en: Pleased to meet you, Wilmer. From Jinotega itself or from thereabouts?
options.feedback: Asking whether it is the town or the department is a local question, and it tells him you know the north is not one place.

options.es: Mucho gusto. Yo soy de aquí de Managua.
options.en: Pleased to meet you. I am from here in Managua.
options.feedback: A fair swap, and after four years you have earned de aquí. He will still hear where you started.

options.en: Jinotega? And is that in Nicaragua?
options.feedback: It is three hours away and it grows most of the coffee in the country. That question does not land as a joke.

steps.speaker: Wilmer
steps.es: De un cafetal por allá arriba. Hablo despacio, dicen aquí.
steps.en: From a coffee farm a bit further up. I talk slowly, they say here.

options.es: Despacio sí, pero yo todavía le agarro poco. Tenga paciencia.
options.en: Slowly yes, but I still only catch a bit. Bear with me.
options.feedback: Honest and it puts you both on the same side. Slower and harder to follow at once is exactly what a different department sounds like.
You do not, yet. Saying so now means the next four sentences go past unrepaired.

options.en: It is that you talk oddly.
options.feedback: He talks like Jinotega. To him it is Managua that talks oddly, and he is being polite about it.

steps.speaker: Wilmer
steps.es: Es que allá se habla distinto. Cada departamento tiene lo suyo.
steps.en: Up there they talk differently. Every department has its own.

options.es: Yo creía que era un solo acento en todo el país.
options.en: I thought there was one accent for the whole country.
options.feedback: Admit the wrong idea out loud. The country is small enough to cross three departments in a morning and they do not sound the same.
Fine. He was offering to explain the north to you and you said you already had it.

options.es: Managua es el acento correcto, pues.
options.en: Managua is the correct accent, though.
options.feedback: Said to a man from the north on his first morning, that is a poor start and it is not true either.

steps.speaker: Wilmer
steps.es: Ideay, y usted no es de aquí tampoco, ¿verdad?
steps.en: Ideay, and you are not from here either, are you?

options.es: No, pero ya llevo cuatro años. Los dos venimos de afuera.
options.en: No, but I have been here four years now. We both come from somewhere else.
options.feedback: He has just put the two of you in the same boat on purpose. Taking it is worth more on a first morning than anything you could say about yourself.

options.es: No, yo vengo de más lejos que usted.
options.en: No, I come from much further away than you.
options.feedback: True, and it makes the distance the point. He was offering you something else.
It is, and always will be a bit. He asked kindly and there was a warmer answer available.
